verdict.rationale: OpenRouter provides model fallback routing that automatically retries the next model in a priority list when a provider errors, is rate-limited, or down, plus load-balanced provider routing for uptime—effectively covering transient provider error resilience. However this is framed as model/provider fallback rather than a configurable 'retry policy' with retry counts/backoff, and there's no evidence of granular retry-policy controls (e.g., retry same model N times) or documentation of failure/latency thresholds beyond model swapping.
